pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: The task processor for sending email verification now first checks if the user's email is already verified before proceeding. If the email is verified, the task is skipped without creating a new verification record or sending an email.

behavior_changes.description: Email verification tasks for users who already have a verified email address no longer create verification records or send verification emails; the processing is short-circuited and the task completes successfully with a logged info message.
evidence: In worker/task_send_verify_email.go, a new if-check was added to ProcessTaskSendVerifyEmail that returns early if user.IsEmailVerified is true.
The early return is logged indicating the verification email task was skipped.
The associated test TestProcessTaskSendVerifyEmail with sub-test "AlreadyVerified" verifies this behavior by mocking the store and mailer to expect no creation or sending calls.

important_symbols.reason: This method implements the core behavior change related to skip processing for already verified emails.
This test validates the changed behavior, confirming no database creation or email sending occurs when email already verified.

investigation_hints.description: Verify how clients or the task scheduling system handle skipped verification tasks and if any downstream systems expect verification emails to be sent unconditionally.

local_risks: Skipping the creation of verification records or sending emails for already verified users is safe only if no workflow depends on re-sending verification emails.
The new code assumes the user object correctly indicates verified status and that no database inconsistencies will cause false negatives.
Logs must be monitored to ensure skipped tasks are intentional and not hiding errors such as stale user state.
uncertainties: Whether any callers or systems downstream expect a verification email to be sent regardless of user state is not evident from the diff.
Whether this impacts retry logic or visibility into verification attempts in operational dashboards is not visible here.
The exact lifecycle and timing of verification tasks in the broader system, including scheduling and retries, cannot be determined from this diff.
Any additional side effects triggered by verification email sending beyond database creation and mailer interaction are unknown.
